annotation.title_clean: New report and guidelines for indigenous data sovereignty in artificial intelligence developments
annotation.title_en: New report and guidelines for indigenous data sovereignty in artificial intelligence developments
annotation.summary_en: UNESCO news page announcing a report and guidelines on indigenous-people-centred AI in Latin America and the Caribbean. It urges participatory inclusion, indigenous data sovereignty, free prior and informed consent, and public policies, and it highlights five Mexican AI language and cultural projects. No embodied AI content.
key_provisions_or_claims: Indigenous peoples have the right to self-determination and to govern their data.
Digitization of indigenous data requires free, prior and informed consent.
Privacy and intellectual property rights must be ensured, including against misappropriation of cultural patterns.
Public policies should integrate indigenous perspectives in all phases of AI development.
Five Mexican best-practice cases cover language learning, translation and textile cataloguing.
